## 22. Swift packages design

One Swift package in `ios/sdk/`, `Package.swift` at its top (PD19), iOS 17 (PD11), products `CraftBridge` and `CraftBridgeEffects` (PD16). The engine start needs no processor check on iOS: every chip iOS 17 runs on (A12 and newer) has FP16. Apps reach it by local path during development and through `craftbridge-swift` from the first release (D-24).

| Target | Change | What |
|---|---|---|
| `CraftBridgeFFIBinary` | NEW | `binaryTarget(path: "Frameworks/CraftBridgeFFIBinary.xcframework")`, named for the target and never for a crate, since the layer table says which library it holds (§15), built by `tools/build-xcframework.sh` and never committed; `craftbridge-swift` carries `url:` and `checksum:` instead (`evidence/05-mobile-platforms.md` Finding 10, D-24) |
| `CraftBridgeFFI` | NEW, generated | UniFFI Swift for both crates, in `Sources/CraftBridgeFFI/Platform/Generated/`, where AGENTS §4's pointer rule holds (§20) |
| `CraftBridge` | NEW | the core's Swift API |
| `CraftBridgeEffects` | NEW | the EffectCraft API: hand-written fixed-shape calls plus `Generated/` (§21) |
| `CraftBridgeEffectsTests` | NEW | Swift Testing: the conformance corpus on the simulator (QA-2) |

**`CraftBridge` (core, hand-written):**
- `JSONValue` (`Codable`, literals), which crosses the boundary as JSON text, and `CraftError` (UniFFI's, with `LocalizedError` messages in the core's own words, read through `craft_error_message`, §14). `CraftError`, `Folders` and `ProgressListener` are named from `CraftBridge` itself.
- `Folders.appDefault`: `Application Support/CraftBridge/{config,models,staged}` — the staged folder beside `config` and `models`, never under `Caches`, which iOS may empty while the app is not running and a saved project must still find the copies it names —, `Caches/CraftBridge`, the app's sandbox (`NSHomeDirectory()`) as the write root, so an export may go into `Documents`, which the Files app shows for an app that shares it, as well as `Library` or `tmp` — the start proves it can write there through the working folders' probes, since the top of the sandbox takes no new file on a device (§16) — and `Bundle.main` as the read-only root; `plugins` only through `Folders.appDefault.allowingPlugins(in: "PlugIns")`, a folder inside the bundle (PD13).
- `ClosureProgressListener`, the `ProgressListener` adapter from a closure of `done`, `total` and `secondsLeft`; `ExportJob` with `cancel()` and an `async` `result`; cancelling the `Task` that awaits the result sets the `CancelToken`.
- `Engine.attachMetalLayer(_ layer: CAMetalLayer)`, under `Platform/`: the one place a layer becomes `Unmanaged.passUnretained(layer).toOpaque()`, with its parameter typed `CAMetalLayer` since the Rust side trusts the class and takes a retain of its own (§20). `PreviewTarget` keeps the layer an app previews into and whether the engine still holds it; `engine.preview(_:into:at:)` attaches the layer when it must and draws the frame of a composition at a time (`Duration`), and `engine.endPreview()` gives the surface up.
- `FrameBytes.pixelBuffer()` (under `Platform/`) → `CVPixelBuffer` (`kCVPixelFormatType_32BGRA`, IOSurface-backed, sRGB) and `FrameBytes.cgImage()` → `CGImage`, each from a frame asked for as `Bgra8Premultiplied`, whose bytes they hold as the core wrote them; any other format is refused.
- `BackgroundPolicy`: `.cpuWhenBackgrounded` (default: `suspendGpu` on entering the background, `resumeGpu` on return) or `.keepGpu` for apps running a `BGContinuedProcessingTask` with the GPU entitlement (§17, §25). `BackgroundController` applies it for the life of the engine (`EffectsEngine.start(folders:gpu:background:)`), and for whichever policy keeps every export out of suspension: each runs under a background task from its start to its end, and is cancelled when the system is about to stop the app. This holds whatever folders the engine was started in: a running export holds the pending-export journal's file lock, which iOS punishes in a suspended app when the config folder is in an App Group, and the GPU device it took at its start, whatever `suspendGpu` drops.

**`CraftBridgeEffects`:** `EffectsEngine.start(folders:gpu:background:)` and the fixed-shape calls, each a thin call into the engine method of §14's table that answers it: `exec`, `run`, `props`, `get`, `set`, `frame`, `export`, `replay`, `timings` and `mcp` are members of `EffectsEngine` itself, and `templates.open` and `templates.render` are hand-written extensions of the generated `templates` namespace's own type, so `engine.templates.open(…)` keeps that shape. `templates.open` answers a `TemplateInstance`, whose `set(_:_:)` and `set(_:media:)` run the commands `template.open`'s own values run — `essential.set` on the instance, in its own composition, after `file.import` for a media file — since §14's table has no method that sets a control of an instance already open. A public member written by hand never takes the base name of a public member the facade generates on the same type, neither a namespace's word on `EffectsEngine` nor a command's name on a namespace's type, since Swift would let a method with arguments stand beside either; the `swift_build` stage refuses one (AGENTS §9). These are the calls used in §5.

**Build.** `tools/build-xcframework.sh` runs `cargo xtask generate`, whose registered generator writes the Swift bindings into `Platform/Generated/` (§20), then `cargo xtask xcframework`, which builds the library the layer table gives the SDK (§15; `craftbridge-effects-ffi` while it has one app) with `--release` for `aarch64-apple-ios` (for the A12, the oldest chip iOS 17 runs on, whose half-precision instructions gemm-f16 needs: the CPU target `tools/env.sh` sets once for every device build, the gate's mobile stage and the device runner included) and `aarch64-apple-ios-sim` with `IPHONEOS_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=17.0`, and joins the two static libraries, each with the crates' headers and one module map, with `xcodebuild -create-xcframework` into `ios/sdk/Frameworks/`. A static library carries no link flags, so each module map also links the system frameworks and libraries its library calls into, which an app's link then takes. Each fact is read from what owns it: the targets are the Apple targets `rust/rust-toolchain.toml` lists, the iOS version and the framework's folder are the package's manifest's, each library's file is the one Cargo reports building, and what it links is rustc's own answer for that library (`--print native-static-libs`), so a framework new platform code calls into is linked with no other edit. The framework is joined again only when a library Cargo rebuilt or a header changed, since a new one makes every Swift build that links it rebuild what imports it. The gate builds it before the two stages that compile the package's Swift, `swift_build` and `swift_lint`, with `--keep-bindings`, which leaves the committed Swift as it is so that the `generated` stage still finds a hand edit; the rules read the package through its manifest, which needs no native library.

**States.** Development (`ios/sdk/` by local path, the local XCFramework) · release (`craftbridge-swift` by URL, the XCFramework downloaded and checksum-verified by SwiftPM).

**Tests.** Every target built in Debug and Release for the iOS device and the iOS Simulator in the gate; the corpus in Swift Testing on the iPhone simulator (QA-2) and on the acceptance iPhone (QA-3).
